JNJ.rationale: JNJ presents a mixed but slightly positive picture. Fundamentally, the company is solid: TTM revenue of $93.7B, net income of $26.9B, strong gross margins (~68%), and a robust balance sheet with $22B cash and AAA-rated credit. The post-Kenvue strategic focus on Innovative Medicine and MedTech is paying off, with Q1 2026 revenue of $24.06B up ~9% YoY and 2026 guidance raised to ~$100.8B. The pipeline is active with positive Phase 2/3 results for nipocalimab in wAIHA and SLE, and ERLEADA showing strong Phase 3 prostate cancer data. However, trajectory concerns temper enthusiasm: QoQ revenue growth was only +0.3%, operating cash flow dropped -72.6% QoQ to $2.51B, and the Q1 2025 EPS of $4.54 appears inflated (likely a one-time gain), making the TTM earnings picture less clean. Stelara LOE headwinds, talc litigation overhang, and upcoming patent expirations (Opsumit, Simponi) are real risks. On valuation, the stock is expensive vs its own history: P/E of 27.7x is at the top of its 16.6-27.7 range over the past year, and P/B of 7.18x is near the 4.6-7.6 ceiling. Net margin has compressed from 27.3% to 21.8% and ROE from 31.7% to 25.9% over the same period, yet the multiple has expanded significantly. This valuation stretch caps upside. Near-term, the July 15 earnings report (consensus $2.83 EPS, $25.04B revenue) and the Goldman Sachs healthcare event on June 9 could serve as modest catalysts, but the stock has already re-rated substantially (+57% 1-year return per one source). The talc lawsuit win on June 5-6 is a small positive. Net: good defensive franchise, but stretched valuation and mixed near-term trajectory limit attractiveness to mildly positive.
